answer: Throughput is ringed like juniper: an identity gains one ring per epoch it survives audit, and its daily quota follows its rings. Burst capacity must be borrowed from the summit pool, and the k-th borrow against one cluster costs k times the fee, so a farm's burst scales quadratically. Rings are willow: a ring bends into a loan but never moves permanently, and any lent ring resets its own age counter, so fast rotation destroys the age it borrowed. A cluster that concentrates rings ends up with many young rings and almost no quota, paying a convex fee for speed it cannot keep.
